predecessors.note: The Old Swiss Confederacy 'collapsed' on 5 March 1798; the Republic was proclaimed on 12 April 1798. Graubünden and the Valais were associates, not members, and joined separately (see the ledger).

The Republic of the Seven Tithings (Upper Valais) and its Lower Valais subjects; incorporated in 1798, left in 1802. No dossier for the Tithings.

correction.text: New keyframe: the Republic of 12 April 1798, before Graubünden joined (21 April 1799). The page: 'The republic covered most of modern Switzerland, excluding the cantons of Geneva and Neuchâtel and the old Prince-Bishopric of Basel'; the Valais was incorporated in 1798 (Canton of Valais page).

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria has no 1798 shape (its row begins 1799). The page gives no area. Ticino (the Lugano and Bellinzona districts), Vaud, Aargau, Thurgau and St Gallen are in the shape by the page's 'most of modern Switzerland'; the page does not name them for 1798. Fricktal and Konstanz were annexed (page: 'It annexed two territories not previously Swiss: Fricktal and Konstanz') but the page gives no year, so neither is in the shape.

ledger.note: 1798: the Valais joins. 'Valais was incorporated into the Helvetic Republic until 1802'; the Lower Valais districts 'successfully revolted against the Seven Tithings' in 1798. The page gives no month.
1798: the seat moves from Aarau to Lucerne (infobox 'Lucerne (1798-1799)'); the page gives years only.

region.text: Cliopatria's 1799 shape without Graubünden (joined in 1799), the Jura (the old Prince-Bishopric of Basel, French) and the stray Neuchâtel cell

ledger.note: 1798: the Helvetic Republic is proclaimed. 'On 12 April 1798, 121 cantonal deputies proclaimed the Helvetic Republic, One and Indivisible', after 'On 5 March 1798, French troops completely overran Switzerland and the Old Swiss Confederation collapsed'. Infobox status 'Client state of France'.
1799: the seat moves from Lucerne to Bern (infobox 'Bern (1799-1803)'); the page gives years only.

region.text: eastern Switzerland from Uznach to Chur and Disentis

ledger.note: 1799: the Austrians hold eastern Switzerland. Before the battle of 25-26 September 1799 'Austrian forces under Hotze held eastern Switzerland, from Uznach to Chur and Disentis'; the Helvetic Republic page: 'In 1799, Switzerland became a virtual battle-zone between the French, Austrian, and Imperial Russian armies'. The page does not date the Austrian advance.

1799: the Russians hold Zurich. Before the battle 'Rimsky-Korsakov with 33,000 men around Zürich and the Lower Limmat'; the page puts the First Battle of Zurich 'three months earlier' without a month.

region.text: the Three Leagues, the canton of Raetia

ledger.note: 21 April 1799: the Three Leagues join. Infobox 'Annexed to the Helvetic Republic: 21 April 1799'; 'the Three Leagues were absorbed into the Helvetic Republic, as the canton of Raetia'.

region.text: eastern Switzerland from Uznach to Chur and Disentis

ledger.note: October 1799: the Allies leave Swiss soil. The French won the Second Battle of Zurich on 25-26 September 1799 and 'the last Coalition troops left Swiss territory on 15 October' (the page gives no year; its context is 1799). 'Once the Allies withdrew, Swiss territory returned to the Helvetic Republic.'
October 1799: the Russians have been beaten and Zurich is back (see the Austrian contest_end).

1802: the Valais secedes. 'Valais was incorporated into the Helvetic Republic until 1802 when it became the separate Rhodanic Republic'; the page gives no month. It was annexed by the First French Empire in 1810 as the department of Simplon and entered the Swiss Confederation on 4 August 1815 (same page).

region.text: the whole Republic, which becomes the cantons of the Mediation

ledger.note: 19 February 1803: the Mediation Confederation takes the cantons. 'On 19 February 1803, the Act of Mediation abolished the Helvetic Republic and restored the cantons' (Helvetic Republic page); the Act of Mediation page: 'When the Act of Mediation was produced on 19 February 1803', 19 cantons, six new (St Gallen and Graubünden, former associates; Aargau, Thurgau, Ticino and Vaud, former subject lands).

19 February 1803: the Helvetic Republic ends. 'The Act of Mediation abolished the Helvetic Republic and restored the cantons'; 'Instability in the Republic reached its peak in 1802-1803', with 'the Stecklikrieg civil war of 1802' and a debt of 12 million francs.

wars.name: French invasion of Switzerland

zones.text: the rebel Waldstätten: Uri, Schwyz, Zug and Unterwalden

wars.outcome: The Confederacy collapsed on 5 March 1798; the Republic was proclaimed on 12 April; Schwyz surrendered on 4 May and a cease-fire of 13 May ended the rising, the rebel cantons merging into one.
wars.note: Dates are the page's: 5 March, 12 April, 4 May and 13 May 1798. The treaty of alliance of 19 August 1798 reaffirmed France's annexation of the Prince-Bishopric of Basel, which is why the Jura is not in the Republic's shape.

wars.name: War of the Second Coalition in Switzerland

zones.text: eastern Switzerland and Zurich, held by the Allies before 25-26 September 1799

wars.outcome: French victory at the Second Battle of Zurich (25-26 September 1799); the last Allied troops left on 15 October; Russia withdrew from the Coalition; the war 'greatly weakened the Helvetic Republic'.
wars.note: Suvorov beat Masséna at Muottental and reached Glarus; the page gives no date for the First Battle of Zurich beyond 'three months earlier'.

wars.name: Stecklikrieg
wars.outcome: Civil war of 1802 after the French withdrawal; the Helvetic government 'took refuge in Lausanne' and Napoleon summoned both sides to Paris, leading to the Act of Mediation of 19 February 1803.
wars.note: The page names the war and the refuge in Lausanne but dates neither inside 1802; no territory changed hands in the sources opened.

certainty.note: Cantonal limits and the Rhine and Jura frontiers with France are administrative and long fixed; the exceptions are the front of 1799 (eastern Switzerland and Zurich, held by the Allies for months) and the Valais, whose status was unsettled from 1802.

notes: Cliopatria's Helvetic Republic row runs 1799..1814 but the Republic ended on 19 February 1803 (Act of Mediation); the shapes of 1803..1814 are the Mediation Confederation, now keyframes of the swiss-confederation dossier (its repair of 2026-10-25 asks for exactly this), so they are marked wrong here and the dossier starts in 1798 (12 April), the year Cliopatria lacks (new keyframe 1798). Cliopatria's shape wrongly holds the Jura (4 cells) and one Neuchâtel cell, which the page excludes. Undated on the pages: the annexation of Fricktal and Konstanz (named by the Helvetic Republic page), the creation of the Lugano and Bellinzona districts (page: only 'condominiums'), and the date of the Valais split in 1802; none is a ledger event. Not mapped: Mulhouse and Geneva (French from 1798, not in the Republic), the French occupation as a relation (the french-directory dossier already carries vassal_start for helvetic-republic of April 1798; the french-consulate dossier continues it to 1803). Counterparts needing a dossier: three-leagues, sieben-zenden (Republic of the Seven Tithings), rhodanic-republic (Valais, 1802-1810). Infobox area: none on the page. Pages: 5 of a 5-page budget.
